\"24Narketpally50 \u003Cb\u003EAltered Sensorium Outcomes\u003C\/b\u003E \u003Cb\u003ETriad\u003C\/b\u003E\":\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1. *\u003Cb\u003EInfection Detection\u003C\/b\u003E*: Infectious etiologies are a common cause of altered sensorium (25 cases), emphasizing the importance of prompt identification and management of sepsis, meningitis, and other infections.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2. *\u003Cb\u003EComorbidity Consideration\u003C\/b\u003E*: Comorbidities like diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease are significant risk factors (30 cases), highlighting the need for thorough evaluation and management of underlying conditions.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3. *\u003Cb\u003EAppropriate Testing and Treatment*\u003C\/b\u003E: Avoidance of non-evidence-based testing and treatment is crucial (20 cases), stressing the importance of judicious use of lab tests, antibiotics, and sedatives to prevent harm and optimize outcomes.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThese three learning points form the \"\u003Cb\u003E24Narketpally50 Altered Sensorium Outcomes Triad,\u003C\/b\u003E\" providing a concise summary of key takeaways for improving patient care.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBased on the data, the admission and discharge dates are not evenly spaced out over the study period from October 2022 to April 2024. Instead, there are clusters of admissions and discharges in certain periods, indicating that the first clinical encounters were not uniformly distributed throughout the study period.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHere's a rough breakdown of the timeline:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- October 2022 to December 2022: Few admissions and discharges (less than 5)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- January 2023 to March 2023: Increased admissions and discharges (around 10-15)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- April 2023 to June 2023: Few admissions and discharges (less than 5)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- July 2023 to September 2023: Increased admissions and discharges (around 10-15)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- October 2023 to December 2023: Few admissions and discharges (less than 5)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- January 2024 to April 2024: Increased admissions and discharges (around 10-15)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe periods with fewer admissions and discharges (October 2022 to December 2022, April 2023 to June 2023, and October 2023 to December 2023) suggest that the first clinical encounters were less frequent during these times, likely due to the convenience sampling approach adopted by the investigators.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe clusters of admissions and discharges in the other periods (January 2023 to March 2023, July 2023 to September 2023, and January 2024 to April 2024) may indicate that the investigators had increased access to patients during these times, potentially due to factors like increased clinic hours, more research staff availability, or targeted recruitment efforts.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr and blogs"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;RISK FACTORS, CLINICAL SPECTRUM, DIAGNOSTIC AND OUTCOME PREDICTORS OF PATIENTS WITH ENCEPHALOPATHY\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBY\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;DR. HARI PRIYA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPOST GRADUATE IN GENERAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EKAMINENI INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EKALOJI NARAYANA RAO UNIVERSITY OF HEALTH SCIENCES\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELoading…\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EINTRODUCTION\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•ENCEPHALOPATHY is a broad term for any diffuse disease of the brain that alters brain structure or function. The hall mark of encephalopathy is altered mental status.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•Encephalopathy may be caused by bacteria, virus, or prion, metabolic or mitochondrial dysfunction, ischemic or hypoxic ,brain tumour or increased intracranial pressure, long standing exposure to toxic substances like \u0026nbsp;drugs, radiation, solvents, paints, industrial chemicals, and certain metals, trauma, \u0026nbsp;poor nutrition, or lack of oxygen or blood flow to the brain. \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•In febrile illness, multiple pathogenic mechanisms can contribute to the encephalopathy. Pathological process can directly affect the central nervous system or indirectly affecting the central nervous system through systemic complications such as hypovolemia, hypoglycaemia, hypoxia, anaemia, hepatic failure, renal failure and bleeding.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•Clinically it is synonymously used with multiple terminologies including altered sensorium, altered mental status and change in mental status.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•It is important to understand normal mental status to identify patients with altered mental status.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EINTRODUCTION\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELoading…\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•MENTAL STATUS is a combination of patient’s level of consciousness and cognition.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•Normal mental status is when the patient has normal level of consciousness and the content of consciousness is normal. Consciousness is the quality or state of being aware especially of something within oneself.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•The terms used to describe different level of consciousness are\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.NORMAL OR ALERT\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.DROWSY OR LETHARGIC\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.VIGILANT OR HYPERALERT\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4.STUPOR\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5.COMA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EINTRODUCTION\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•The Content of consciousness include\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.ORIENTATION\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2.ATTENTION\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3.EXECUTIVE FUNCTION\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4.LANGUAGE\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5.MEMORY\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6.PERCEPTION\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•Normal mental status when impaired \u0026nbsp;is termed altered mental status which can be either an altered level of consciousness \u0026nbsp;ranging from being vigilant or hyper alert to being drowsy, stupor or comatose or an impairment in the content of the consciousness or a combination of both.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EINTRODUCTION\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•ALTERED MENTAL STATUS (AMS) is used to describe different states of mental functioning that can vary between mild confusion to coma.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•Different synonyms are used in the literature to describe this state such as, not acting right, confusion, altered behaviour, altered sensorium, lethargy, agitation, psychosis, disorientation, inappropriate behaviour, in attention.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•The understanding of these terminologies will help us in identification of the problem early and also to document it accurately so that further worsening or improvement can be assessed.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EINTRODUCTION\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAIM :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•TO STUDY THE RISK FACTORS , CLINICAL SPECTRUM AND OUTCOMES OF PATIENTS PRESENTING WITH ENCEPHALOPATHY\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOBJECTIVES:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•To study the risk factors \u0026amp; etiology of patients presenting with encephalopathy\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•To study the clinical and laboratory predictors in the diagnosis of etiology (Infectious and non-infectious) of encephalopathy\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•To assess the outcome (Mortality and functional outcome) of patients with encephalopathy .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E• To study the predictors of outcome in patients with encephalopathy\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMATERIALS \u0026amp; METHODS:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPLACE OF STUDY: GENERAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT, KAMINENI INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESTUDY PERIOD: OVER 2 YEARS ( OCT 2022 – AUG 2024)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESTUDY DESIGN : PROSPECTIVE OBSERVATIONAL STUDY\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESAMPLE SIZE: 50 PATIENTS\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESAMPLE POPULATION: PATIENTS OF AGE 18- 65YRS ATTENDING MEDICINE DEPARTMENT IN KAMINENI INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCE\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELoading…\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•The study has been approved by the ethics committee of kamineni institute of medical sciences, narketpally.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•All patient satisfying the inclusion criteria will be enrolled in the study.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•A written informed consent will be taken from the patients prior to the start of the study\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EINCLUSION CRITERIA:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1. Patients with age from 18years-65years.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2. Written informed consent from each patient or legal guardian prior to enrolment patients age 18-65 years\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3. All patients with signs \u0026amp; symptoms suggestive of encephalopathy(defined as any form of altered sensorium\/altered level of consciousness)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEXCLUSION CRITERIA:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•1.Patients with Age less than 18 years\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•2.Patients who haven’t given Consent\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•3. Patients who are not capable of giving consent (mentally ill patients)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•4. Patients in encephalopathy with focal neurological deficit\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMETHODOLOGY:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•30 random patients (n=30) who were hospitalized for altered sensorium as well as satisfied our inclusion \u0026amp; exclusion criteria were selected for this study.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•All patients underwent full medical and neurologic clinical evaluation and Glasgow Coma Scale grading at the time of admission (time of admission to study was arbitrarily taken as the time of first neurologic assessment).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•Laboratory investigations included complete blood count, renal function test, serum electrolytes,random blood sugars,liver function test, urine routine examination. ECG and X-Ray chest were done for all patients. CSF examination (in suspected cases of meningo encephalitis), CT \u0026amp;MRI brain and other investigations were done as and when required.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMETHODOLOGY:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•Patients were neurologically evaluated daily and the progression was monitored with Glasgow Coma Scale scoring.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•All patients were followed till discharge and at one month.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E• Outcome was graded and recorded into 2 categories:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•I – Death (Mortality)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•II – Good recovery\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•The history, general examination, the neurological profile at the time of admission, important positive investigation findings, the diagnosis and outcome of all cases are presented in tabular form (master chart) and analysed.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPROFORMA:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;• Serial No.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;• Name:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;• Age:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;• Occupation:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;• Address :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;• OP NO.\/IP NO.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;• D.O.A:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;• D.O.D\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPROFORMA:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EETIOLOGY:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EINFECTIOUS\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMETABOLIC\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•HYPERTHERMIA\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•HYPONATREMIA\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•HYPERGLYCEMIA\/HYPOGLYCEMIA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•HYPOXIA , HYPERCAPNIA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•HEPATIC\/UREMIC ENCEPHALOPATHY\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•TOXINS –ALCOHOL RELATED,DRUGS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPROFORMA:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPROFORMA:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOUTCOMES:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•MORTALITY\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•MORBIDITY AT DISCHARGE AND AT ONE MONTH.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOBSERVATION \u0026amp; RESULTS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E•A total of 30 patients with altered sensorium admitted to our hospital kamineni institute of medical sciences were studied over a period of 1 year and the following results were obtained.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETABLE NO 1: AGE WISE DISTRIBUTION (n=30)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAGE\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETOTAL\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E18-20\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E21-30\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E31-40\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E41-50\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E7\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E51-60\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E61-70\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E71-80\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E81-90\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECHART
